clue.text: Like permissive society, impervious to current licentiousness ?

definitions.text: Like permissive society, impervious to current licentiousness ?

parts.words: Like permissive society, impervious to current licentiousness
parts.note: a permissive society cannot be outraged by today's loose morals, and a device built to be impervious to electric current has the same compound description

explanation.surface: A social commentator describes the permissive society as unmoved by the loose morals of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present-day', but it also hints at electric current: a well-insulated tool is proof against electric current, just as a permissive society is proof against outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unable to be scandalised or jolted is literally proof against shocks, whether moral or electrical.

clue.text: Enclosure of the clan next month

definitions.meaning: an old word for a railed enclosure or fence
a branch of a clan, especially in Ireland or Scotland
the abbreviation for the month after August

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a fenced enclosure, a branch of a clan, and the short written form of the ninth month of the year.

clue.text: Crab catchers ?

parts.note: in rowing, to catch a crab is to fumble a stroke when the blade jams in the water, so the things doing the catching are the rowers' blades

explanation.surface: A question about the fishermen who trap shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch a crab' is a rowing idiom for a botched stroke where the blade sticks in the water; the catchers are not fishermen but the rowing blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing blades are what catch a crab, the rowing term for a fouled stroke.

clue.text: Strokes of the pen that open bars ?

definitions.text: Strokes of the pen that open bars ?

parts.words: Strokes of the pen that open bars
parts.note: in written music the sharps and flats penned at the start of the stave tell the player which notes to adjust in every bar that follows

explanation.surface: Pen strokes, such as a licence signature, that allow pubs to open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs opened by a signed licence; here they are bars of music, opened by the sharps and flats written at the start of each stave.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharps or flats at the head of a stave fix the tonality for the music's bars.

clue.text: "Ee!" let out the heroine as it madly charged

definitions.text: "Ee!" let out the heroine as it madly charged

indicators.note: the two letters of the exclamation are released, dropped from the word that follows
the remaining letters behave madly, rearranging themselves into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the word heroine

explanation.surface: A melodrama heroine shrieks as some wild beast charges at her.
explanation.walkthrough: Take EE out of HEROINE to leave HROIN, then 'madly' rearranges those letters. The whole clue also pictures the animal charging, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large horned African beast notorious for charging wildly at anything that alarms it.

clue.text: Horse and cart turn out for the players

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters are turned over and set out in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse and cart are brought out for a troupe of travelling actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' hints at actors, but here they are musicians; 'turn out' rearranges HORSE plus CART.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of instrumentalists playing together is a symphonic ensemble of musicians.

clue.text: Sort of bar bird

definitions.meaning: a crowbar is a type of iron lever bar
a black corvid, such as a rook or jackdaw

explanation.definitionFit: The word prefixes a lever bar and also names a common black corvid.

clue.text: Charon's craft goes along with 2

parts.note: Charon, ferryman of the Greek underworld, propels his little vessel across the Styx with the blades that answer clue 2

explanation.surface: The ferryman of the dead's boat moves along with the help of a couple of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Charon is the ferryman who rowed the dead over the Styx; his craft is propelled by the answer to 2-down, the blades a rower pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Charon's ferry is a small vessel propelled by blades pulled by hand rather than sail or engine.

clue.text: He has what it takes to make a packet

definitions.text: He has what it takes to make a packet

parts.words: He has what it takes to make a packet
parts.note: to make a packet sounds like getting rich, but a pay packet is just the weekly envelope of wages a worker takes home

explanation.surface: A go-getter who has the talent to make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a packet' means get rich, but read literally a pay packet is made up from the wages that an ordinary salaried worker takes home.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in paid employment who receives a regular wage, the stuff of a pay packet.

clue.text: One's turn on special occasions to make a political truce, say

parts.note: party is the noun for a political group, used here as a modifier

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a truce is a peace between warring sides

explanation.surface: A diplomat's move on a special occasion to broker a truce between political rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: A political truce would be a 'party peace'; 'say' tells you to hear PEACE as PIECE, giving a performer's favourite turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a performer's set routine, trotted out at gatherings and celebrations.

clue.text: Catch on, but don't trust your weight to it

definitions.text: don't trust your weight to it
definitions.meaning: a slender ... on a tree would snap if you stood or hung on it

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for grasping a point, and also a thin branch too frail to hold a person.

clue.text: Early school is more benevolent with information about art

parts.note: kinder is the comparative of kind, meaning more benevolent

indicators.note: about places one word around another, so the information wraps the art

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: An early-years school is described as kinder and better informed about art.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'about' wraps it around ART to give GARTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery class for young children before formal primary education begins.

clue.text: Not a characteristic of those who take orders

definitions.text: Not a characteristic of those who take orders

parts.words: Not a characteristic of those who take orders
parts.note: people who take orders follow commands, so refusal to comply is the trait they lack; there is a hint at monks taking holy orders too

explanation.surface: A remark about the qualities of those who take holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take orders' can mean become a priest or monk, but read plainly it means obey commands, so the missing trait is refusal to comply.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusal to obey commands is exactly what a compliant subordinate does not show.

clue.text: Impromptu speaker reads his notes so

definitions.text: Impromptu speaker reads his notes so

parts.words: Impromptu speaker reads his notes so
parts.note: a speaker without prepared text might scribble prompts on his shirtsleeve and read them from there

explanation.surface: How an unprepared speaker reads out his scribbled notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for unrehearsed speech comes from jotting notes on a shirt cuff, so the speaker literally reads from that spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without preparation is said to be done as if reading jottings from one's shirtsleeve.

clue.text: Joyful addition to the faithful, come Christmas ?

definitions.text: Joyful addition to the faithful, come Christmas ?

parts.words: Joyful addition to the faithful, come Christmas
parts.note: the Christmas carol opens 'O come, all ye faithful, joyful and ...', so the word that follows joyful completes the line

explanation.surface: A happy new member joins the congregation at Christmas time.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol 'O Come, All Ye Faithful' runs 'joyful and triumphant'; the clue's 'faithful', 'come' and 'joyful' all quote that line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word follows joyful in the carol's opening line and means jubilant or exulting.

clue.text: One of twenty-six in the year

definitions.text: One of twenty-six in the year

parts.words: One of twenty-six in the year
parts.note: a year of fifty-two weeks splits into twenty-six periods of two weeks each

explanation.surface: Something that occurs twenty-six times a year, like a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty-six suggests the alphabet, but fifty-two weeks divided into pairs gives twenty-six two-week spans.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-week period, of which a fifty-two-week year holds twenty-six.

clue.text: There's a great change about some fuel-store

indicators.note: change about tells you to shuffle the letters round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big reorganisation is under way at a fuel depot.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GREAT and SOME, rearranged by 'change about', make a nine-letter fuel tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tank that held town gas, a familiar landmark of old British towns.

clue.text: Exclude the fancy bread

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are arranged ornately

explanation.surface: A diner refuses a posh loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like it describes the bread, but it rearranges the letters of BREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone formally from a place or activity is to shut them out.

clue.text: Faith ! The Americans have laws against it

definitions.text: The Americans have laws against it
definitions.meaning: in the USA antitrust laws forbid business cartels, called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Means confidence or belief, and is also a business cartel, which American antitrust law outlaws.

clue.text: Old man did not pray to be thrown down here

definitions.text: Old man did not pray to be thrown down here

parts.words: Old man did not pray to be thrown down here
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme 'Goosey Goosey Gander', the old man who would not say his prayers is taken by the left leg and thrown down the stairs

explanation.surface: An old man who refused to pray is punished by being hurled down.
explanation.walkthrough: This alludes to the English nursery rhyme 'Goosey Goosey Gander': 'There I met an old man who wouldn't say his prayers, I took him by the left leg and threw him down the stairs.'
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps with its banisters, the place the old man was thrown down in the rhyme.

clue.text: Tentative suggestion that a former fairy's round the bend

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
a peri is a fairy in Persian mythology
round the bend is slang for mad, as is mental

explanation.surface: Someone tentatively suggests that a fairy of old has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: A PERI is a fairy from Persian legend; 'round the bend' is British slang for crazy, here MENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on trial or by way of a test is provisional rather than final.

clue.text: Musical work unpopular with trawlermen ?

definitions.meaning: a fisherman would dislike having ..., read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A piece written for nine performers, and also, split in two, the lack of a net a fisherman dreads.

clue.text: Jacobson gives the continental half a dozen

parts.note: le is French for the, so a continental the
six is VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A man called Jacobson donates six of something to a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacobson' looks like a surname, but it is a son of Jacob: one of the twelve sons in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the patriarch Jacob had twelve sons, the third by Leah giving his name to a priestly tribe.

clue.text: Party man

definitions.meaning: a ... party is a groom's night out before his wedding
a male deer, or a man going unaccompanied by a woman

explanation.definitionFit: Describes a men-only pre-wedding party, and also a male, as in a man attending alone.

clue.text: On high like a tree

parts.note: up means on high or aloft
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: Something is perched high up, like a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The upas is a Javanese tree with poisonous sap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical Asian tree whose poisonous sap was once used on arrows.

clue.text: Inappropriate way to give drinks at a sit-in ?

definitions.text: Inappropriate way to give drinks at a sit-in ?

parts.words: Inappropriate way to give drinks at a sit-in
parts.note: a sit-in protest has everyone seated, so paying for a round described as a standing one would not suit the occasion

explanation.surface: A question about buying a round for demonstrators at a sit-in.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'stand treat' is to pay for everyone's drinks; at a sit-in, where everyone is seated, standing anything is out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for a round of drinks or a meal for others, an idiom built on the verb stand.

clue.text: That's your lot !

parts.note: said when a supply runs out, but one's lot in life is also the destiny allotted to one

explanation.surface: A server announcing the rationing is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's your lot' sounds like 'that's all you get', but 'lot' also means one's destiny in life.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is the destiny or fortune one is dealt in life.

clue.text: Soft about caring for someone? Playing possum ?

parts.note: p, short for piano, means soft in music
re means about or concerning
tending means looking after or caring for

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted carer asks whether someone is faking illness.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft; 'playing possum' means feigning death or sleep, as the opossum does.
explanation.definitionFit: To play possum is to feign death or sleep, faking a state one is not in.
